chunks: 2493 - And it is narrated from Ayyub ibn A‘yan, who said:
I heard al-Walid ibn Sabih saying to Abi Abdullah عليه السلام: “Abu Hanifah saw the crescent of Dhu al-Hijjah at al-Qadisiyyah and attended ‘Arafah with us.”
So he said: “There is no salat (prayer) for this; there is no salat (prayer) for this.”

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdullah, the Imam addressed in the narration
key_terms.أَيُّوبُ: Ayyub, the named narrator transmitting the report
key_terms.الْوَلِيدَ: al-Walid, the person relating the statement to the Imam
key_terms.ذِي الْحِجَّةِ: Dhu al-Hijjah, the month of hajj (pilgrimage)
key_terms.صَلَاةٌ: salat (prayer), whose validity is being negated in this statement
key_terms.عَرَفَةَ: ‘Arafah, the rite/day associated with the standing during hajj (pilgrimage)
key_terms.هِلَالَ: the crescent moon, marking the beginning of the lunar month

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام say about acting on Abu Hanifah’s sighting of the Dhu al-Hijjah crescent?
ai.summary: This hadith relates a report presented to Imam Abu Abdullah عليه السلام concerning Abu Hanifah’s sighting of the crescent of Dhu al-Hijjah at al-Qadisiyyah and his standing at ‘Arafah accordingly. The Imam عليه السلام responds by negating the validity of the salat connected to that act, indicating a legal judgment concerning the correctness of the procedure followed.
